newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Juncker sees euro-zone stability council.
newsitem.headline: Juncker sees euro-zone stability council.

text.p: European Union countries joining monetary union will need a special council to co-ordinate policies after the launch of the single currency, Luxembourg Prime Minister Jean-Claude Juncker said on Monday.
He said he saw no reason for a row over a French proposal to set up an informal stability council after the launch of the euro in January, 1999.
The proposal has come under fire from the Bundesbank, which fears it might be used to undermine the independence of the future European Central Bank (ECB).
"We will have this stability council as we had the stability pact," Juncker, who is also Luxembourg's finance minister, told reporters as he arrived for a meeting of EU finance ministers.
EU leaders agreed in December on a budget discipline pact meant to ensure monetary union members keep deficits low after the launch of the euro.
"I do not understand the reaction from several people (to the stability council proposal)," Juncker said. "There is no reason at all for becoming nervous."
It was "common sense" for countries inside the euro-zone to hold informal councils, similar to the Group of Seven rich nations' talks, to co-ordinate policies.
"I can't see there are any reasons for a row at all. There is no reason for any watering down of the independence of the central bank," he said.
He said he did not have the impression the German government was opposed to the stability council idea.
"I've seen that the Bundesbank had a strong reaction, but as far as I could see, the German finance minister did not," he said.
